title: Honest Bands for Untrimmed ATE Estimation under Weak Overlap with Multiple Endpoints
banked_reason: Independent MAIN validity confirms terminal below-field: accepted re-rooted matched honest-length package is incremental, paper-score ceiling 4.8 < 7.4 with no bounded field upgrade. Preserve advisory-versus-typed-halt distinction, stale original-promise finding, related-work gap and under-attested Heiler-Kazak assumptions; no completed source/soundness/Lean certification.
gap_reasons: The delivered note establishes matched n^(-2/5) honest expected-length order, but does not deliver the specified full-class bivariate AIPW stable limit, fitted-mark calibration, or identical-marginal calibration counterexample. Its scalar obstruction specializes [Heiler–Kazak's published result](https://pure.au.dk/ws/files/307676406/Heiler_Kazak_JoE_2021_AM.pdf), while the faster construction applies familiar smoothness-based bias accounting rather than establishing a broadly useful new inference method. The rate proof combines constant-reproducing boundary weights, second-moment coverage, and a localized two-point lower bound; the simultaneous contrast family reduces to two contrasts, and the lower bound uses identical endpoints. The TL;DR correctly distinguishes matched order from the open sharp constant, so there is no stale sharp-constant overclaim. The lower and upper length constants differ by more than 2,600-fold, leaving the practical efficiency of the proposed band unresolved. The exact known design, narrow assignment family, and absence of supporting coverage or length computations constrain the projected paper score; these delivered results constitute a specialized extension rather than a field-level contribution. [D0.5.G projected paper-score gate: paper_score_ceiling 4.8 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'subfield' is capped at 'incremental'. The score assesses the delivered research package without credit for unfinished work.]

The proposed flagship was a uniform bivariate paired-mark stable calibration, including rank-collapse coverage and the identical-marginal critical-value diagnostic; this node delivers only scalar stable limits, while the core expressly defers every requested joint-calibration component.

The claimed minimax n^{-2/5} order is a theorem-level contribution, but its novelty and closest rate-literature comparison are not established: publication priority is expressly deferred and the relevant minimax comparator listed in the bibliography is not substantively compared.

The supplied Proposition 3.2 text verifies a stable-limit conclusion only under Assumptions 3.1 and 3.5--3.8; it does not attest that this node's expanded primitive likelihood, integrability, and tail conditions are exactly those assumptions, so the cited invocation used by the subclass audit is not yet discharged.
proof_attempt_summary: The accepted D-0.5 re-root replaced the original joint fitted-mark calibration program with a published-estimator subclass obstruction, a finite-sample honest boundary procedure, and an informal matched n^(-2/5) honest-length order proof on the restored residual-TV class. The later independent general review graded this package incremental with score ceiling 4.8 below the fixed field floor 7.4; fresh MAIN validity confirms no bounded field upgrade and directs a downgraded stop, while the raw panel halt remains REVISE/kernel_substituted rather than a clean PASS. Full Heiler-Kazak numbered-assumption attestation, substantive minimax-prior-art comparison, the stale topic mismatch, and the sharp leading constant remain unresolved; no Lean formalization, source/soundness certification, promotion, presentation or Git commit occurred.
tldr: On the restored public class with unknown quadratic propensity, Lipschitz outcome regressions, boundary residual-TV regularity, and a coordinate moment floor, the untrimmed population ATE estimator in Heiler and Kazak equation (3.2) has nondegenerate \(n^{1/3}\)-scale error on an audited legal Bernoulli subclass. Bands centered at that estimator with common width \(o_P(n^{-1/3})\) therefore fail uniformly. A total boundary-reweighted procedure has finite-sample simultaneous \(0.90\) coverage and half width at most \(130n^{-2/5}\). Moreover, the optimal honest expected common band length satisfies \((31/320)n^{-2/5}\le\mathfrak L_n\le260n^{-2/5}\), so the rate exponent is minimax optimal. Only existence, value, and attainment of the sharp leading constant remain open.
gap: The scalar stable limit of the published untrimmed DR score does not determine the honest width available when the same population ATE is restricted by public Lipschitz smoothness. A comparison needs the actual published score and learners, an explicit legal adverse family, and a finite honest alternative in the identical experiment.
fill: Theorem 3 establishes both sides of a strict \(1/15\) exponent separation against Heiler and Kazak equation (3.2) on the shared class. Theorem 1 audits the published scalar limit on a common subclass; Theorem 2 gives the explicit total boundary procedure and finite sample constants; Open-ended Question 1 asks for sharp honest length in that experiment.
